name: High-Press 4-3-3

slots.why: Sweeper keeper covers the space behind the high line and starts moves with his feet.
Support wing-back gives width and joins the press high up the pitch.
Ball-playing defender steps out to press and starts attacks with a pass.
Cover centre-back sweeps behind his partner, since the line is high; Defend is the alternate.
Attacking wing-back gives the width on the right and pushes on when the ball is won.
Ball-winning midfielder harries opponents in the middle and wins the ball back.
Box-to-box midfielder supports the press and runs beyond the striker when the ball is won.
Mezzala runs into the half-space to arrive in the box.
Winger presses the full-back and stays wide when the ball is won.
Inside forward cuts in to shoot and attack the box.
Pressing forward leads the press by closing down the defenders. Advanced Forward is the alternate.

description: An aggressive 4-3-3 designed to regain possession high and sustain pressure in the opposition half.
whyGood: The front three, energetic midfield and compressed defensive line make it easier to surround the ball.
whyThisShape: A 4-3-3 built around a high, aggressive press: a ball-winning midfielder in front of the defence, energetic midfielders alongside him, and a pressing forward leading three attackers. The team wins the ball high and finishes attacks quickly.
whenToUse: When you have fit, energetic players and want to play in the opponent's half, especially against sides that build slowly from the back.
whenNotToUse: Against sides that play long over the press, or when your players lack stamina: the press cannot be kept up for 90 minutes.

instructionRationale.Much Higher Line of Engagement: Begin pressure close to the opposition build-up and goalkeeper.
instructionRationale.Much More Urgent Pressing: Use a very urgent settled press; assess recoveries, chances allowed and fitness rather than assuming it succeeds.
instructionRationale.Higher Defensive Line: Move the back line up to reduce the space behind the midfield and support territorial pressure.
instructionRationale.Shorter Passing: Use the short connections supplied by the selected midfield and supporting forwards.
instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Challenge immediately after losing possession, with the roles around the ball supporting the first pressure.
instructionRationale.Counter: Use the forward runners immediately after a regain, before the opponent can recover its shape.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Full Backs: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Roll It Out: Start possession through the chosen short outlets instead of routinely contesting a long kick.

setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
